equivalent: Zero by construction, through three steps the one-clause version of this argument skipped. (1) THE SUBTRACTION IS THE RIGHT ONE ONLY BY A BIT-EXACTNESS INVARIANT. The accept test is `e_flip < e_now`, while the recorded line differences `e_flip - last`. They agree because `last` is bit-identical to `e_now` at every accepted flip: `last` starts as `start = Dense::energy(cue)` and `dots` is initialised by the same per-pattern fold, so the first `e_now = -sum f(dots)` is bit-identical to `start`; and after an accepted flip the incremental `*d -= 2.0 * p[i] * x[i]` is character for character the expression `e_flip` was evaluated on (`f(d - 2.0 * p[i] * x[i])`, with the pre-flip `x[i]`, since `x[i] = -x[i]` runs after the dots update), and the next `e_now` folds the same terms in the same order. So `e_flip - last` IS `e_flip - e_now`, and that is strictly negative: `e_flip < e_now` excludes equality, excludes `-inf` against `-inf` (`-inf < -inf` is false) and excludes NaN (every comparison false), and two distinct finite f64 never subtract to zero. The running max therefore never leaves its `+0.0` initial value. The `last == Dense::energy(state)` half of that identity is asserted directly by `the_dense_plateau_is_a_fixed_point_and_the_running_energy_is_the_energy` and by `the_dense_energy_monitor_differences_the_energy_it_accepted_and_reports_a_positive_zero`. (2) WHAT THE MUTANT ACTUALLY COMPUTES. `0.0 * (a strictly negative double)` is `-0.0`, not `0.0`, so the mutant evaluates `0.0f64.max(-0.0)`, whose result Rust documents as non-deterministic for inputs that compare equal. Measured on this crate's arm64 target (Darwin 27, Apple Silicon): `0.0f64.max(-0.0)` is `+0.0` in both operand orders, so the mutant's `worst_increase` is `+0.0`, bit for bit the original's -- and `+0.0 == -0.0` would have hidden the difference from every `assert_eq!` in any case. The new fixture asserts `is_sign_positive()` and the `{:?}` rendering, so a target whose `max` returns the second operand for equal zeros will report this mutation as `caught` instead of leaving this claim silently false. (3) THE INFINITE CASE. If `e_flip` is `-inf` with a finite `last` (reachable at a large `degree`, where `f` overflows), the original records `-inf` and the mutant computes `0.0 * -inf = NaN`. They still agree: measured, `0.0f64.max(f64::NAN)` is `0.0` (max ignores NaN) and `0.0f64.max(-inf)` is `0.0`. Equivalent on every target where `f64::max` returns `+0.0` for `(+0.0, -0.0)`, which is what IEEE 754's maxNum recommends and what the fixture above now measures rather than assumes.
